## Summary

**Written**: `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (overwrote the unpopulated scaffold)

**Version**: `1.0.0` — initial ratification. The prior file was a pure template with no values, so no governance was in force to amend; this is the first real version rather than a MAJOR bump from something.

**Structure**: four principles, matching the four you supplied — the template's fifth principle slot was dropped rather than filled with invented content.

| Principle | Teeth it was given |
|---|---|
| I. Standard Library Only (NON-NEGOTIABLE) | Runtime imports stdlib only; `pytest` carved out as the sole dev-only dependency, and runtime code may not import it |
| II. Fail Loudly | stderr + non-zero exit for CLIs, raise/explicit error result for APIs; bare `except` and `except: pass` forbidden; no masking defaults or partial results |
| III. Every Requirement Is Testable | Each functional requirement maps to ≥1 pytest test, named explicitly; error paths tested too; untestable requirement = not yet specified |
| IV. Simplicity | Smallest design that meets the spec; no speculative extension points; complexity must cite the requirement forcing it |

Two supporting sections make the principles enforceable: **Additional Constraints** (Python 3.11+, stdlib-only runtime, stdin/args → stdout convention, no hidden global state or stray filesystem writes) and **Development Workflow & Quality Gates** (a four-item pre-completion gate, plus the rule that a plan introducing a third-party runtime dependency is rejected absent an amendment).

**One tension worth flagging**: Principles I and III collide, since pytest is itself third-party. I resolved it by writing the exception into Principle I explicitly — pytest is permitted as a development dependency only, and runtime code must not import it, so removing the dev environment cannot change runtime behavior. If you'd rather the project stay literally dependency-free and use `unittest`, that's a MINOR amendment to Principle I and III.

**Deferred items**: none blocking. `PROJECT_NAME` was inferred generically as "Python Project" — the repo has no README or packaging metadata declaring a name. Rename it on the first amendment if you pick a product name. `RATIFICATION_DATE` is set to today (2026-11-14) rather than marked TODO, since this is the first adoption.
